messages.subject: how to manipulate spacing
parts:
Dear All,

I have five levels of x values which are not equally spaced. But I
want to put them eqaully spaced in a scatter plot with a connecting
line.

For example,
test = data.frame(x = c(4, 8, 16, 32, 64), y = c(1:5))
And I want to draw a following type of graph
qplot(x, y, data = test) +geom_line()
but x values should be equally spaced.

I tried to use factor(x) but I cannot draw the connecting line.

Thank you,

messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: Re: how to manipulate spacing
parts:
On 2010-09-09 12:57 PM, Soyeon Kim wrote:
> Dear All,
>
> I have five levels of x values which are not equally spaced. But I
> want to put them eqaully spaced in a scatter plot with a connecting
> line.
>
> For example,
> test = data.frame(x = c(4, 8, 16, 32, 64), y = c(1:5))
> And I want to draw a following type of graph
> qplot(x, y, data = test) +geom_line()
> but x values should be equally spaced.
>
> I tried to use factor(x) but I cannot draw the connecting line.

In the general case, you need something like this:

ggplot(test, aes(x=factor(x), y=y, group=1)) +
geom_point() + geom_line()

The "group=1" part is key - leave it out and you won't get a line. If
your real x-values have the same pattern as they do in the example data
set you gave, though,

ggplot(test, aes(x=x, y=y)) +
geom_point() + geom_line() +
scale_x_log2()

would be better.

zw
